reading.title: The Bean Sprout Experiment
reading.purpose: Follow Diego as he turns a question about bean seeds into an experiment with numbers.
paras: Diego wondered how likely it was that a bean seed would sprout. His teacher, Ms. Reyes, smiled. "Let us turn that question into an experiment," she said. Diego felt uncertain, because some seeds sprout and others never do.

Each student planted ten seeds in paper cups. To keep the test fair, Ms. Reyes chose the spots for the cups on the windowsill at random, pulling numbers from a hat. Every planting was one trial, one try of the experiment, and Diego kept a tally on a chart, marking a stroke each time a seed sprouted.

After a week, the class compared charts. It had been an average week, neither very hot nor very cold. Most students had between seven and nine sprouts, a tight cluster of numbers close together. Diego found the class average by adding up all the sprouts and dividing by the number of students. It came to about eight out of ten.

"So the probability that a seed sprouts is about eight out of ten," Diego said. "The chance is high, but not certain." Ms. Reyes nodded. "Probability is a number that tells the likelihood of something happening. A few cups cannot prove it, but more trials make our answer better."
Diego grinned. "Next time I will plant a hundred seeds," he said.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, a "cluster" of numbers is
choices: one number that is much larger than the rest
a list of numbers written from least to greatest
a group of numbers close together
a chart that records every number in the class
qs.why: The text says the sprout counts formed "a tight cluster of numbers close together."

qs.q: Which sentence shows how the cups were placed fairly?
choices: To keep the test fair, Ms. Reyes chose the spots for the cups on the windowsill at random, pulling numbers from a hat.
Each student planted ten seeds in paper cups.
Diego felt uncertain, because some seeds sprout and others never do.
After a week, the class compared charts.
qs.why: Pulling numbers from a hat gave every cup an equal chance at every spot, which keeps the test fair.

ev.text: To keep the test fair, Ms. Reyes chose the spots for the cups on the windowsill at random, pulling numbers from a hat.

qs.q: Why does Diego say the chance is "high, but not certain"?
choices: Only two out of ten seeds sprouted in the experiment.
Every seed sprouted in every cup that the class planted.
The class planted too few cups to count anything at all.
About eight out of ten seeds sprouted, so some did not.
qs.why: Eight out of ten is a high chance, but because two did not sprout, a seed is not guaranteed to grow.

qs.q: What is the best summary of this story?
choices: A teacher picks the best seeds for her class to plant.
A student tests how likely a seed is to sprout.
A class forgets to water its seeds and has to start over.
A class grows a hundred bean plants for a school garden.
qs.why: Diego asks how likely a seed is to sprout, runs trials, finds an average, and describes the probability.

clues.text: marking a stroke each time a seed sprouted
adding up all the sprouts and dividing by the number of students
